title: Further referenced sources (citation only — data not redistributable)

citation.title: Curated bibliography of transmission-line EMF measurement and simulation studies
citation.article_license: Citations only. No third-party data reproduced.

method.note: This document carries no field data. Each entry below points at a published source whose licence does not permit redistribution of its data inside Taki. Use the digitising template in the Validation tab to enter values from the published figures yourself, then compare as user data with the source recorded.

provenance_notes: NO DATA IS SHIPPED IN THIS FILE. Only the Fikry et al. (2022) dataset is bundled with values, because its underlying data carries an explicit CC0 public domain dedication. Every other source identified during the review is either paywalled or all-rights-reserved.

Reproducing measurement tables from those papers inside Taki would be a copyright violation, and inventing plausible-looking numbers in their place would be far worse — it is exactly the failure mode that made the old synthetic 'Standard Benchmark' curves worthless. Neither is done here.

The workflow instead is: pick a source below, open it, digitise the published lateral profile into the CSV template, and load it as user data with the citation attached. Taki then treats it as a fully cited reference and records the provenance in the validation report.
Entries marked kind='measured' are the valuable ones for model validation — they test whether Taki reflects physical reality, which no amount of code-to-code verification can establish.

bibliography.title: Magnetic field measurement from 132/275 kV overhead power lines
bibliography.relevance: Direct field-meter measurements on Malaysian 132 kV and 275 kV lines. The closest available match to Taki's primary use case, and the highest-value target for model validation.
bibliography.units_note: Confirm whether values are reported in microtesla or milligauss before entry. 10 mG = 1 uT.

bibliography.title: Measuring and simulation of magnetic field generated by high voltage overhead transmission lines
bibliography.relevance: Carries BOTH measured and simulated values with an ICNIRP comparison, so a single source supports code-to-code verification and model validation simultaneously. Also the source establishing that Malaysian Standard MS 2332-1:2009 sets the public limit at 100 uT.
bibliography.units_note: Verify the DOI against the article record before citing in a deliverable — it was not confirmed during the initial review.

bibliography.authors: See Journal of Nuclear and Related Technologies record
bibliography.title: Measurement of extremely low frequency (ELF) magnetic flux density in the vicinity of overhead high-voltage transmission lines at UKM
bibliography.container: Journal of Nuclear and Related Technologies (Nuklear Malaysia)
bibliography.relevance: Lateral-profile measurements near 132 kV and 11 kV lines on the UKM campus, using a field meter and the standard lateral-profile methodology. Peak reported 12.5 mG (1.25 uT).
bibliography.units_note: Reported in MILLIGAUSS. Convert with 10 mG = 1 uT before entry.

bibliography.authors: Sahbudin RKZ, Fauzi SA, Hitam S, et al.
bibliography.title: Investigation of electrical potential and electromagnetic field for overhead high voltage power lines in Malaysia
bibliography.relevance: Electrical potential and EMF for Malaysian 132 kV and 275 kV double-circuit lines. One of the geometry sources underlying the bundled Fikry et al. dataset.

bibliography.title: Computation of magnetic field from quadruple tower transmission lines in Malaysia
bibliography.container: Proceedings of the Universities Power Engineering Conference (UPEC)
bibliography.relevance: Quadruple-circuit tower magnetic field computation, including the phase-pattern groupings the transposition conventions derive from.

bibliography.authors: Rahman NA, Mahadi WNL, Said I, et al.
bibliography.title: Simulation approach in evaluating the electromagnetic fields from the new lines of Extra High Voltage (EHV) circuits near residential area in Malaysia
bibliography.relevance: EHV field simulation at multiple Malaysian sites for 132/132 kV quadruple and 500 kV double-circuit lines, specifically near residential areas.

bibliography.title: Recommendation ITU-T K.90: Evaluation techniques and working procedures for compliance with exposure limits of network operator personnel to power-frequency electromagnetic fields
bibliography.relevance: The recommendation behind the EMFACDC solver used by Fikry et al. The authoritative place to resolve the outstanding sqrt(2) normalisation question recorded against that dataset.

bibliography.title: How to calculate the magnetic field from a three-phase circuit
bibliography.relevance: The in-phase / out-of-phase decomposition used by Fikry et al. Also publishes standard line geometries usable as further verification cases. Directly relevant to the unresolved sqrt(2) discrepancy.

bibliography.authors: International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection
bibliography.title: Guidelines for limiting exposure to time-varying electric and magnetic fields (1 Hz to 100 kHz)
bibliography.relevance: Primary source for the 200 uT / 5 kV/m general-public reference levels in standards.py.

bibliography.title: IEEE Std 644: Standard Procedures for Measurement of Power Frequency Electric and Magnetic Fields From AC Power Lines
bibliography.relevance: The correct methodology standard for field measurement, including probe height and lateral-profile procedure. Cite this rather than IEEE Std C37.1, which Fikry et al. appear to reference in error for the 1 m measurement height.
